One Municipality, Two Kinds of Demolition, One Flat Price for Both

c: East Gwillimbury’s demolition work splits pretty cleanly along the line between old and new. In the century hamlets — Holland Landing, Sharon, Mount Albert, Queensville — it’s usually a small structure that came with an old property, taken down with the patience an established home deserves. Along the 404 corridor and Green Lane’s newer streets, it’s a different kind of job entirely: an above ground pool, a deck or a shed that’s only a few years old but already needs to come down for a bigger renovation, because fast-growing households tend to hit that point quickly. On the concessions between the two, it’s fence lines and outbuildings on working farm properties, cleared the same flat way whether the address is a hamlet or a highway exit. The 700+ five-star reviews behind Live Junk Free come from every version of that split — the same crew, the same price, whichever side of the municipality the job’s on.
